en: The *Sutra on the Five Kinds of Meritorious Retribution for Giving Food* is also titled the *Buddha-spoken Sutra on Bestowing Physical Strength and Beauty*.
The translator’s name is lost; it is now appended to the catalog of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the assembly of bhikṣus:
"One should know that moderation in eating is called 'diminution' (損).
The Buddha said:
'When a person takes food and gives it to others, there are five merits. If a wise person weighs their intentions and makes their resolve vast and expansive, then there are five paths of merit.'"
What are the five? First is the gift of life;
second is the gift of beauty; third is the gift of strength; fourth is the gift of peace; and fifth is the gift of eloquence.
"What is meant by 'bestowing life'?
All sentient beings establish their physical lives in dependence upon food; if they do not obtain food, they will pass away in seven days at the most. Therefore, to bestow food is to bestow life."

As for those who give life, they shall enjoy long life in every successive birth within the heavenly worlds; their lives shall not be cut short prematurely, and their clothing, food, and wealth shall be naturally provided in immeasurable abundance.
What is meant by "giving form"?

One who receives food gains a radiant complexion; when one does not receive food, they become angry and their appearance loses its luster, becoming withered and unsightly. Therefore, one who gives food bestows a radiant complexion.

As for those who give the gift of physical beauty, they will be handsome and upright in every lifetime, whether born in the heavens or the human world; their appearance will be so radiant as to be rare in the world, such that all who see them cannot help but gaze upon them and bow their heads in reverence.
"What is the power of giving?

When a person obtains food and drink, their physical strength becomes robust, and they can move, advance, or retreat without difficulty. One who does not obtain food suffers from hunger, thirst, and the distress of heat, becoming breathless and emaciated. Therefore, to give food is to give power."

As for the power of giving, one possesses great strength in life after life; born in the heavenly worlds, one’s strength is peerless, and in every movement—whether entering or exiting, advancing or halting—it never declines or diminishes.
What is meant by "giving peace"?

When a person receives food, their body becomes peaceful and secure, and they suffer no distress; whereas one who does not obtain food feels sorrow in mind and peril in body, remaining unsettled in sitting or rising and unable to find stability. Therefore, to bestow food is to bestow peace.

Those who practice giving and bring peace will be free from affliction life after life; their minds will be at ease and their bodies strong. Reborn in the heavens or the human world, they shall not suffer various calamities. Wherever they go, they will always encounter the virtuous and good; possessing immeasurable wealth, they shall not meet with premature death or injury.
"What is meant by 'bestowing eloquence'?

One who receives food has their vital energy replenished and their will strengthened, such that their speech becomes fluent and unimpeded. One who does not receive food has their body weakened and their will diminished, such that they cannot discuss matters and find it difficult to speak. Therefore, bestowing food is to bestow eloquence."

As for those who bestow eloquence, they shall be intelligent and wise in every lifetime, whether born in the heavens or the human world; their speech shall be eloquent and insightful, their verbal fluency seamless and free from any flaw, such that all who hear them will rejoice and look up to them with reverence.
These are the five meritorious gifts.

If one generates the aspiration for enlightenment and gives to all beings, having obtained this merit, in every place where they are born, they will always see the present Buddhas and receive instruction in the profound Dharma: the four immeasurables, the four ways of winning over others, the six perfections, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the manifestation of the Dharma-body, and infinite life-span with distinct marks and signs. Possessing the thirty-two major marks, they attain the ten powers to achieve the Buddha-way, establishing great peace and universally rescuing those in peril. With wisdom and eloquence, they produce billions of voices to deliver and liberate the worlds of the ten directions.
When the Buddha had spoken this sutra, the assembly of bhikṣus, the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and the fourfold disciples were all filled with joy; they paid their respects and departed.
The Sutra on the Five Kinds of Auspicious Rewards for Bestowing Food.
